Lecture 13

A particle in space: orbital angular momentum

Orbital angular momentum acts on wavefunctions in three dimensions. We decompose their space into finite-dimensional multiplets and prove that only integer spins occur. Harmonic polynomials give spherical harmonics, and central potentials reduce to a radial rule. The oscillator provides two counts of the same level.

Lecture 13, first part

Orbital angular momentum and its integer spins

13.1 Three dimensions

13.3 The multiplets on functions

The multiplet theorem of Quantum Mechanics I, Thm 7.3, needs a finite-dimensional space that the operators map into itself. The LjL_jLj​ act on S(R3)\mathcal S(\R^3)S(R3), which is infinite-dimensional. So we look for finite-dimensional subspaces of S(R3)\mathcal S(\R^3)S(R3) that the LjL_jLj​ keep. The LjL_jLj​ do not change the degree of a homogeneous polynomial, and they commute with multiplication by a function of ∣x∣\abs x∣x∣. So the polynomials of one degree, times the Gaussian below, make such a subspace.

Lecture 13, second part

Spherical harmonics and the radial rule

13.4 Spherical harmonics

The first part proved that L2(R3)\Ltwo(\R^3)L2(R3) is an orthogonal sum of multiplets of L\mathbf LL, and that every spin in it is an integer. In this part we write the multiplet of spin lll with harmonic polynomials and lower its top vector to obtain the spherical harmonics. We then read the radius and the direction of a particle, reduce a central potential to a rule on the half-line, and count the oscillator’s levels twice.

The direction is read in a similar way. Let AAA be a cell of the sphere, given by intervals of θ\thetaθ and φ\varphiφ. Multiplication by the indicator of the set where x^∈A\hat x\in Ax^∈A is an orthogonal projection, so it is an observable, and its reading answers whether x^\hat xx^ lies in AAA. For ψ=(u/r)Y\psi=(u/r)Yψ=(u/r)Y as above, the probability of yes is ∫A∣Y∣2 dΩ\int_A\abs Y^2\,\dd\Omega∫A​∣Y∣2dΩ, whatever uuu is. Figure 13.4 shows ∣Y∣2\abs Y^2∣Y∣2 for l≤1l\le1l≤1. The density of Y00Y_{00}Y00​ is uniform, that of Y10Y_{10}Y10​ vanishes on the equator, and that of Y11Y_{11}Y11​ vanishes at the two poles.

Theorem 13.10 (Spherical harmonicscited). The YlμY_{l\mu}Ylμ​, l≥0l\ge0l≥0, ∣μ∣≤l\abs\mu\le l∣μ∣≤l, form an orthonormal basis of L2(S2)\Ltwo(S^2)L2(S2). Every ψ∈L2(R3)\psi\in\Ltwo(\R^3)ψ∈L2(R3) is a sum, convergent in norm, ψ(x)=∑l,μulμ(r)r Ylμ(θ,φ),∥ψ∥2=∑l,μ∫0∞∣ulμ(r)∣2 dr,\psi(x)=\sum_{l,\mu}\frac{u_{l\mu}(r)}r\,Y_{l\mu}(\theta,\varphi), \qquad\norm\psi^2=\sum_{l,\mu}\int_0^\infty\abs{u_{l\mu}(r)}^2\,\dd r ,ψ(x)=l,μ∑​rulμ​(r)​Ylμ​(θ,φ),∥ψ∥2=l,μ∑​∫0∞​∣ulμ​(r)∣2dr, and ψ↦(ulμ)\psi\mapsto(u_{l\mu})ψ↦(ulμ​) is a unitary map onto the sequences of functions in L2(0,∞)\Ltwo(0,\infty)L2(0,∞) with a finite sum of squared norms.

This is Hall, Thm 17.12 and p. 382, and Teschl, Thm 10.7 and (10.45)–(10.49). Both proofs approximate continuous functions by polynomials (Hall by the Stone–Weierstrass theorem, Teschl by Weierstrass’s), and the decomposition of L2(R3)\Ltwo(\R^3)L2(R3) integrates square-integrable functions in spherical coordinates. This course does neither. Theorem 13.6 gives the decomposition of L2(R3)\Ltwo(\R^3)L2(R3) into multiplets without them.

A molecule of HCl rotates almost as a rigid body: the distance ddd between the two nuclei hardly changes. The direction of its axis is a point of S2S^2S2, and its energy of rotation is L2/2IL^2/2IL2/2I, with the moment of inertia I=md2I=md^2I=md2 and the reduced mass mmm of the two nuclei. The YlμY_{l\mu}Ylμ​ have L2=ℏ2l(l+1)L^2=\hbar^2l(l+1)L2=ℏ2l(l+1) and, by Theorem 13.10, form a basis of L2(S2)\Ltwo(S^2)L2(S2), so the levels are ℏ2l(l+1)/2I\hbar^2l(l+1)/2Iℏ2l(l+1)/2I, each 2l+12l+12l+1 times. Absorbing a photon takes the molecule from lll to l+1l+1l+1 (a rule of the coupling to light, not derived here), with the energy ℏ2(l+1)/I\hbar^2(l+1)/Iℏ2(l+1)/I. So the lines are equally spaced, at l+1l+1l+1 times the frequency ℏ/2πI\hbar/2\pi Iℏ/2πI. The lines of H35^{35}35Cl lie at 625.9625.9625.9, 1251.51251.51251.5, 1876.21876.21876.2 and 2499.9 2499.9\,2499.9GHz (Nolt and coworkers, 1987), within 0.2%0.2\%0.2% of the multiples of 625.9 625.9\,625.9GHz. They fall slightly short because the spinning molecule stretches. From ℏ/2πI=625.9 \hbar/2\pi I=625.9\,ℏ/2πI=625.9GHz, I=2.68×10−47 I=2.68\times10^{-47}\,I=2.68×10−47kg m2^22, and with m=0.980 m=0.980\,m=0.980u, d=1.28 d=1.28\,d=1.28Å, an average over the molecule’s vibration (the equilibrium distance is 1.27 1.27\,1.27Å).

13.6 The oscillator in space

Definition 13.12 (The oscillator in space). The Hamiltonian HHH of the isotropic oscillator of mass mmm and frequency ν\freqν, with s=ℏ/mνs=\sqrt{\hbar/m\freq}s=ℏ/mν​, is the operator made, as in Proposition 5.5, from the basis (hn1n2n3)(h_{n_1n_2n_3})(hn1​n2​n3​​) and the numbers ℏν(n1+n2+n3+32)\hbar\freq(n_1+n_2+n_3+\tfrac32)ℏν(n1​+n2​+n3​+23​).

By Proposition 5.5 it is self-adjoint. The rule −(ℏ2/2m)Δ+mν2∣x∣2/2-(\hbar^2/2m)\Delta+m\freq^2\abs x^2/2−(ℏ2/2m)Δ+mν2∣x∣2/2 is the sum of three rules (8.1), one in each variable, so it maps hn1n2n3h_{n_1n_2n_3}hn1​n2​n3​​ to ℏν(n1+n2+n3+32)hn1n2n3\hbar\freq(n_1+n_2+n_3+\tfrac32)h_{n_1n_2n_3}ℏν(n1​+n2​+n3​+23​)hn1​n2​n3​​, by Proposition 8.3. As in the proof of Theorem 8.7, HHH acts by this rule on S(R3)\mathcal S(\R^3)S(R3). The eigenspace of HHH for ℏν(N+32)\hbar\freq(N+\tfrac32)ℏν(N+23​) is ENE_NEN​, since a vector with this eigenvalue has no component on the other basis vectors.

Example 13.13 (The level NNN counted twice).

  1. By coordinates. The level ℏν(N+32)\hbar\freq(N+\tfrac32)ℏν(N+23​) has one basis vector for each triple (n1,n2,n3)(n_1,n_2,n_3)(n1​,n2​,n3​) with n1+n2+n3=Nn_1+n_2+n_3=Nn1​+n2​+n3​=N: for each n1n_1n1​ there are N−n1+1N-n_1+1N−n1​+1 choices of n2n_2n2​, so (N+1)(N+2)/2(N+1)(N+2)/2(N+1)(N+2)/2 in all.

  2. By rotations. By Theorem 13.6, ENE_NEN​ holds one multiplet of each spin l=N,N−2,…l=N,N-2,\dotsl=N,N−2,…, so its dimension is ∑(2l+1)\sum(2l+1)∑(2l+1) over these lll, an arithmetic progression with the step 444, whose sum is again (N+1)(N+2)/2(N+1)(N+2)/2(N+1)(N+2)/2. For example, the level N=2N=2N=2 has 6=5+16=5+16=5+1 states, of spins 222 and 000.

Each level ENE_NEN​ is a sum of whole multiplets (Theorem 13.6), as Quantum Mechanics I, Cor. 7.5, leads one to expect of a Hamiltonian that commutes with rotations. That the spins NNN and N−2N-2N−2 share a level is not forced by rotations. It comes from a larger symmetry of the oscillator, not used here, and Lecture 15 meets the same in hydrogen.

A particle in space

States: L2(R3)\Ltwo(\R^3)L2(R3) is an orthogonal sum of finite-dimensional multiplets of L\mathbf LL, made from polynomials times a Gaussian, and every spin is an integer (Theorem 13.6). Observables: the components of L=Q×P\mathbf L=Q\times PL=Q×P satisfy [L1,L2]=iℏL3\comm{L_1}{L_2}=\ii\hbar L_3[L1​,L2​]=iℏL3​ on S(R3)\mathcal S(\R^3)S(R3) (Proposition 13.4). Away from the origin, the rule of a central Hamiltonian on (u(r)/r)Ylμ(u(r)/r)Y_{l\mu}(u(r)/r)Ylμ​, with uuu smooth, is the radial rule HlH_lHl​ with the centrifugal term (Proposition 13.11). Measurement: a reading of L3L_3L3​ gives ℏμ\hbar\muℏμ with μ\muμ an integer, and a reading of L2L^2L2 gives ℏ2l(l+1)\hbar^2l(l+1)ℏ2l(l+1) with lll an integer; never ℏ/2\hbar/2ℏ/2.

Summary

  • Three dimensions: QjQ_jQj​, PjP_jPj​ and H0H_0H0​ are self-adjoint and act on S(R3)\mathcal S(\R^3)S(R3) by xjx_jxj​, −iℏ∂j-\ii\hbar\partial_j−iℏ∂j​ and −(ℏ2/2m)Δ-(\hbar^2/2m)\Delta−(ℏ2/2m)Δ (Proposition 13.2).
  • Orbital angular momentum: L=Q×P\mathbf L=Q\times PL=Q×P is symmetric on S(R3)\mathcal S(\R^3)S(R3) and satisfies [L1,L2]=iℏL3\comm{L_1}{L_2}=\ii\hbar L_3[L1​,L2​]=iℏL3​ (cyclic), and L3L_3L3​ generates the rotations about the x3x_3x3​-axis (Proposition 13.4).
  • The multiplets on functions: the oscillator’s level ENE_NEN​ is a sum of one multiplet of each spin N,N−2,…N,N-2,\dotsN,N−2,…, and these make up L2(R3)\Ltwo(\R^3)L2(R3); only integer spins occur (Theorem 13.6).
  • Spherical harmonics: the multiplet of spin lll in Pl\mathcal P_lPl​ is the harmonic polynomials, with top vector (x1+ix2)l(x_1+\ii x_2)^l(x1​+ix2​)l (Lemma 13.7); the YlμY_{l\mu}Ylμ​ form a basis of L2(S2)\Ltwo(S^2)L2(S2) (Theorem 13.10, cited). For a unit vector (u(r)/r)Y(u(r)/r)Y(u(r)/r)Y with ∫S2∣Y∣2 dΩ=1\int_{S^2}\abs Y^2\,\dd\Omega=1∫S2​∣Y∣2dΩ=1, the probability of the shell a1<∣x∣<b1a_1<\abs x<b_1a1​<∣x∣<b1​ is ∫a1b1∣u∣2 dr\int_{a_1}^{b_1}\abs u^2\,\dd r∫a1​b1​​∣u∣2dr (Example 13.9).
  • Central potentials: away from the origin, the rule of H0+VH_0+VH0​+V on (u(r)/r)Ylμ(u(r)/r)Y_{l\mu}(u(r)/r)Ylμ​, with uuu smooth, is the radial rule with the term ℏ2l(l+1)/2mr2\hbar^2l(l+1)/2mr^2ℏ2l(l+1)/2mr2 (Proposition 13.11).
